neighbours.label: the completing piece of a fixed name or title that the earlier words make predictable (Who's Who, The Importance of Being Earnest, Jack the Ripper), as against the same words outside the fixed name
fire: The opening night crowd was a veritable who's who of the art world.
His biography was printed in Who's Who in British Science in 1971.
The drama club staged The Importance of Being Earnest in the spring.
Historians still argue about the identity of Jack the Ripper.
The conference speakers formed a who's who of climate research.
My aunt quoted lines from The Importance of Being Earnest at dinner.
She found her grandfather's entry in an old copy of Who's Who in Canada.
The museum has a whole room devoted to Jack the Ripper and Victorian London.
